project.name: openclaw-guide-build
project.description: A comprehensive guide to OpenClaw covering beginner fundamentals, architecture, and production deployment of the local-first personal AI assistant. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: auto-release.yml
nodes.summary: Automates building, testing, verifying, attesting provenance, and publishing PDF and HTML guide editions for tagged releases.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses GitHub Actions with checksum verification for binary dependencies, artifact provenance attestation, and release asset publishing.

nodes.name: ci.yaml
nodes.summary: Continuous integration workflow that executes project tests and rule checks, followed by building and verifying PDF and HTML guide editions on pull requests and pushes to main.
nodes.languageNotes: Orchestrates testing via unittest and custom Python rule checkers, followed by doc build verification using mdPress and Pandoc.

nodes.name: dependabot-automerge.yml
nodes.summary: Automatically enables auto-merge for Dependabot pull requests targeting semver patch updates while leaving minor and major updates for manual review.

nodes.name: identity-guard.yaml
nodes.summary: Server-side git audit workflow that inspects commit authors, committers, and Co-authored-by trailers to prevent AI assistant identities from entering repository history.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements strict regex-based git log stream inspection with fail-closed semantics across push and pull request events.

nodes.name: preview-pdf.yml
nodes.summary: Builds, verifies, and publishes rolling preview editions of the PDF and HTML guides to a mutable preview-pdf release tag on push to main.
nodes.languageNotes: Manages mutable preview releases via GitHub API and CLI with concurrency grouping and checksum validation.

nodes.summary: Explains OpenClaw's architecture using a smart intern metaphor, addressing isolated AI capabilities, multi-channel messaging, and system auditability.

nodes.name: 1.2_scenarios_comparison.md
nodes.summary: Compares OpenClaw with ChatGPT, Cursor, Zapier, and Dify, analyzing token cost implications and practical workload suitability.

nodes.name: 1.3_concepts.md
nodes.summary: Introduces the five core concepts of OpenClaw—Gateway, Agent, Tool, Session, and Node—mapping out the message lifecycle and chapter cross-references.

nodes.name: summary.md

nodes.name: 6.2_context_building.md

nodes.name: 7.2_lark_integration.md

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Serves as the chapter roadmap and table of contents for Chapter 8, introducing architectural governance across lifecycle hooks, cron jobs, heartbeat polling, remote access, and security baselines for 24/7 unattended operations.
nodes.languageNotes: Chapter overview establishing five dimensions of architectural governance required for sustainable unattended operations.

nodes.name: 8.1_hooks.md
nodes.summary: Details OpenClaw lifecycle hooks and event interception points, establishing clear separation of cross-cutting governance concerns like rate limiting, auditing, and data masking while enforcing timeout, degradation, and idempotency constraints.
nodes.languageNotes: Covers gateway hook discovery mechanisms, HOOK.md structure, handler TypeScript files, and diagnostic commands via openclaw hooks.

nodes.name: 8.2_cron_jobs.md
nodes.summary: Guides the design and scheduling of exact-time unattended tasks using built-in gateway cron and external crontab integration, emphasizing idempotency keys, non-overlapping locks, and error triage.
nodes.languageNotes: Differentiates main session events (--system-event) from isolated session tasks (--message) and details jobs.json versus jobs-state.json runtime persistence.

nodes.name: 8.3_heartbeat.md
nodes.summary: Explains OpenClaw's periodic heartbeat mechanism for batched polling and notify-on-demand alerting, dissecting the timer-to-delivery lifecycle, HEARTBEAT_OK protocol, active hours configuration, and token cost optimization.
nodes.languageNotes: Details 250ms debounce merge, per-agent timers, HEARTBEAT.md inspection checklists, and suppression semantics using HEARTBEAT_OK.

nodes.name: 8.4_remote_access.md
nodes.summary: Architects secure remote management for OpenClaw instances using SSH port forwarding, Tailscale Serve private network tunnels, Zero Trust identity principles, and rclone file synchronization.
nodes.languageNotes: Contrasts private Tailscale Serve against public Tailscale Funnel, detailing explicit CLI authentication requirements and remote browser takeover via KasmVNC.

nodes.name: 8.5_security_baseline.md
nodes.summary: Establishes a verifiable defense-in-depth security baseline spanning ingress control, routing bindings, tool execution policies, and secret management with structured audit event logging.
nodes.languageNotes: Formulates a four-tier defense model verified using openclaw doctor, status --deep, and structured JSON log streaming.

nodes.name: summary.md
nodes.summary: Summarizes key operational automation takeaways, provides a practical self-inspection checklist for production readiness, and showcases community deployment patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes self-check items for hooks, cron idempotency, heartbeat quiet hours, remote ingress verification, and previews Chapter 9.

nodes.name: 9.1_architecture_overview.md
nodes.summary: Presents the five-plane architectural framework (Control, Data, Context, Trust, and Visibility planes) for understanding Gateway responsibilities and module boundaries. Analyzes plane interactions, execution surface separation, and cross-plane diagnostic tracing.

nodes.name: 9.2_control_plane.md
nodes.summary: Explores the five core duties and boundaries of the Gateway Control Plane: connection attribution, routing, session lifecycle, policy enforcement, and circuit-breaking failover. Introduces layered approval architecture and practical openclaw.json configuration examples.

nodes.name: 9.3_ws_handshake.md
nodes.summary: Details the full lifecycle of persistent WebSocket connections, covering challenge-response authentication, device identity signatures, keepalive heartbeats, and exponential backoff reconnection. Clarifies the architectural distinction between transport-level connections and stateful sessions.

nodes.name: 9.4_event_idempotency.md
nodes.summary: Examines event idempotency, sequence ordering, and eventual consistency guarantees across distributed agent networks. Explains handling duplicate, lost, or unknown states via idempotency keys, sequence gap detection for snapshot refresh, and session-level mutex locking.

nodes.name: 9.5_pairing_trust.md
nodes.summary: Explains establishing local trust perimeters via device identity registration, nonce-based cryptographic challenge verification, and operator approval workflows. Distinguishes Control Plane device pairing from chat-level DM sender pairing, and outlines token rotation and emergency revocation mechanisms.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Introduces Chapter 9 on OpenClaw Gateway control plane responsibilities, WebSocket connection lifecycles, event consistency, and local device pairing trust. Outlines the chapter outline, pedagogical five-plane architectural framework, and core learning objectives.

nodes.name: summary.md
nodes.summary: Summarizes Chapter 9 key conclusions on control plane arbitration, WebSocket lifecycle management, event idempotency, and device trust bootstrapping. Includes a self-check verification checklist and transitions to Chapter 10 agent loop mechanics.

nodes.name: 10.1_request_lifecycle.md
nodes.summary: Traces the complete end-to-end request lifecycle of an agent message and provides an outside-in layered diagnostic framework for isolating errors across gateway, agent, session, model, and tool tiers.

nodes.name: 10.2_pi_framework.md
nodes.summary: Analyzes OpenClaw's embedded integration of the Pi runtime engine, detailing session lifecycle management, custom tool injection, event subscription bridges, and dynamic system prompts.

nodes.name: 10.3_entry_queue.md
nodes.summary: Details ingress protocol normalization, replay deduplication barriers, and the pure TypeScript lane-based Command Queue governing session, global, and background execution concurrency.

nodes.name: 10.4_prompt_assembly.md
nodes.summary: Examines structured context assembly across four data tiers, token window budgeting with priority-based pruning, prompt persistence audits, and defense-in-depth against prompt injection attacks.

nodes.name: 10.5_tool_execution.md
nodes.summary: Explores the four-stage tool call lifecycle, static policy filtering, dynamic before_tool_call plugin interception hooks, loop detection, and result trimming injection.

nodes.name: 10.6_streaming_retry.md
nodes.summary: Explains the EmbeddedBlockChunker streaming engine with fence-aware markdown chunking, bounded request-level HTTP retry strategies, model failover sequences, and early termination controls.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Serves as the chapter navigation guide for the OpenClaw Agent Loop core, introducing foundational mental models, learning objectives, and reading advice.

nodes.name: summary.md
nodes.summary: Summarizes the key architectural conclusions of Chapter 10, provides a self-assessment checklist across all agent loop mechanisms, and previews Chapter 11 on reliability and security.

nodes.name: 11.1_auth_profiles.md
nodes.summary: Defines the multi-key authentication object model and lifecycle in OpenClaw, covering auth profiles, selection order priority, session overrides, and runtime state tracking. Explains key isolation across environments, zero-downtime key rotation workflows, emergency credential leak response, and audit verification probes.

nodes.name: 11.2_rotation_cooldown.md
nodes.summary: Details the auth profile cooldown and temporary disablement mechanisms designed to prevent retry amplification during provider outages or rate limits. Explains failure count cooldown tiers, exponential backoff for billing failures, and runtime state tracking via auth-state.json.

nodes.name: 11.3_fallback_rules.md
nodes.summary: Establishes explainable model fallback chains and failure triage rules to ensure continuous operation without silent model switches. Covers sequential fallback tiers, context overflow bypass behaviors, half-open probing during cooldown, and fault injection verification techniques.

nodes.name: 11.4_guardrails.md
nodes.summary: Explains the four-layer defense-in-depth guardrail framework combining tool policies, sandbox container isolation, manual execution approvals, and audit logging. Demonstrates prompt injection mitigation, sensitive data masking, and health diagnostic commands.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Chapter roadmap and learning objectives for implementing reliability and security mechanisms in OpenClaw, introducing multi-key governance, cooldown mechanisms, model fallback chains, and defensive guardrails.

nodes.name: summary.md
nodes.summary: Summarizes Chapter 11 key takeaways on explicit multi-key governance, explainable model fallbacks, cooldown circuit breaking, and four-tier guardrail defense. Provides a self-assessment checklist and introduces Chapter 12 on plugin engineering and production operations.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Introduces Chapter 12 on extension engineering and production operations, framing how OpenClaw evolves into an auditable and extensible enterprise platform. Contrasts developer extension mechanisms with Chapter 5's tool user perspective, summarizing plugin lifecycles, custom tools, testing pipelines, and production blueprints.
nodes.languageNotes: Serves as the chapter navigation hub and pedagogical roadmap outlining core developer competencies.

nodes.name: 12.1_plugin_architecture.md
nodes.summary: Details OpenClaw's native plugin architecture, manifest validation mechanics, and five execution modes across agent, message, tool, and gateway lifecycle hooks. Explains two-tier perimeter isolation combining plugin whitelists with tool policies, bundle compatibility with external ecosystems, and CLI diagnostic commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Explains in-process TypeScript runtime extensions, JSON schema pre-validation via openclaw.plugin.json, and five hook execution modes including claim and synchronous hooks.

nodes.name: 12.2_custom_tools.md
nodes.summary: Provides technical guidance for designing and registering custom OpenClaw tools using TypeBox parameter schemas, structured reproducible outputs, and idempotency keys to bound side effects. Demonstrates policy layering where deny rules take precedence, sandbox execution for high-risk actions, and common design anti-patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: Covers TypeBox schema validation, tool registration via api.registerTool, and denying high-risk runtime tool execution across specific chat channels.

nodes.name: 12.3_testing_debugging.md
nodes.summary: Establishes a three-tier verification methodology for extensions spanning plugin loading, policy enforcement, and gateway ingress before end-to-end testing. Introduces snapshot baseline diffing, traceId replay for deterministic fault localization, and automated CI/CD canary release and rollback procedures.
nodes.languageNotes: Features automated snapshot diff scripts, jq log filtering for behavioral baselines, and layered diagnostic CLI commands.

nodes.name: 12.4_production_blueprint.md
nodes.summary: Defines a production blueprint for OpenClaw extensions, enforcing separation of code and configuration changes, three-tier security perimeters, and secret injection via SecretRef. Details emergency rollback runbooks, graceful degradation strategies, and operational KPIs with alert thresholds for gateway latency, resource usage, and tool health.
nodes.languageNotes: Focuses on separating code releases from configuration toggle rollouts, log masking, circuit breakers, and event loop lag monitoring.

nodes.name: 12.5_framework_interoperability.md
nodes.summary: Analyzes interoperability between OpenClaw and frameworks like LangGraph and CrewAI across adapter, protocol, and data layers. Contrasts local embedded, remote service-based, and external bridge topologies, comparing OpenClaw's declarative gateway governance with external state-machine and multi-role orchestration engines.
nodes.languageNotes: Deconstructs three-layer interop architecture across adapter, protocol (A2A/MCP/RPC), and data models (unified message/state/tool results).

nodes.name: summary.md

nodes.name: 14.2_latency_throughput.md

nodes.languageNotes: Breaks down end-to-end request latency into LLM time-to-first-token, tool I/O critical paths, container sandbox lifecycles, and orchestration queue delays.

tour.title: Project Overview and Navigation
tour.description: Start with README.md and SUMMARY.md to understand the scope, target audience, and structure of the OpenClaw guide. As a comprehensive guide for a local-first AI assistant, the repository organizes content across beginner fundamentals, runtime architecture, and production deployment. The book configuration in book.json defines the official navigation sidebar and build settings that structure the entire multi-format documentation suite.
tour.languageLesson: GitBook configuration files (book.json) declare book metadata, plugin dependencies, and multilingual sidebar navigation rules used by static site generators.

tour.title: Foundational Concepts and Primitives
tour.description: Building on the project roadmap, Chapter 1 introduces OpenClaw's primary mental models and architectural abstractions. It frames OpenClaw as an extensible, local-first assistant and formalizes its five core primitives: Gateway, Agent, Tool, Session, and Node. This foundational vocabulary establishes the conceptual contracts that govern how downstream subsystems interact and process user requests.

tour.title: Installation Workflows and Contracts
tour.description: Moving from concepts to concrete setup, Chapter 2 guides users through prerequisites, local daemon management, and Gateway service health acceptance tests. Crucially, the repository pairs user-facing installation docs with an automated test suite in test_installation_contracts.py. This contract test ensures that documented commands, Node.js version constraints, and diagnostic steps stay strictly synchronized with actual software requirements.
tour.languageLesson: Contract testing against documentation files validates that setup instructions, flags, and version bounds do not drift from working reality.

tour.title: Action Layer and Tool Policy
tour.description: With the Gateway service established, Chapter 5 examines OpenClaw's Action Layer, which bridges conversational intent with local system execution. It details tool contract definitions, failure semantics, and the separation between read-only observations and state-mutating actions. The chapter also outlines how tool policies enforce allow/deny precedence and execution permissions across channels to keep autonomous actions strictly governed.

tour.title: Session Lifecycle and Memory
tour.description: Executing tools across long conversations requires robust state management. Chapter 6 explores OpenClaw's session model, thread-level DM isolation, and its dual-tier workspace memory architecture. By separating durable workspace facts in MEMORY.md from transient daily conversation logs, OpenClaw enables continuous contextual awareness while actively bounding prompt token growth.

tour.title: Gateway Protocol and Control Plane
tour.description: Diving into core runtime architecture, Chapter 9 formalizes the five-plane Gateway architecture separating Control, Data, Context, Trust, and Visibility concerns. The Gateway control plane arbitrates client WebSocket handshakes, maintains challenge-response authentication, and guarantees event idempotency across distributed agent nodes. This protocol forms the central communication backbone uniting external chat clients with local agent processes.

tour.title: Agent Loop Runtime Execution
tour.description: Tracing an incoming message through the Gateway brings us to Chapter 10, the engine of the agent runtime loop. This chapter details end-to-end request handling: ingress queueing, four-tier context window assembly, four-stage tool call interception, and response streaming. It highlights defensive runtime components such as the EmbeddedBlockChunker streaming engine for markdown code blocks and bounded HTTP retry mechanisms.

tour.title: Reliability, Fallbacks, and Guardrails
tour.description: To maintain resilience under production workloads, Chapter 11 introduces multi-key authentication governance and defensive guardrails. It establishes auth profile rotation, circuit-breaker cooldowns to prevent retry storms, and four-layer defense-in-depth security combining sandboxing and static policy checks. These patterns ensure explainable model fallbacks without silent failures or security compromises.

tour.title: Diagram Pre-rendering and HTML Reader
tour.description: Having explored the architectural guide content, we now examine the build tooling that compiles and formats the book. The repository includes render_mermaid.py to scan chapters and pre-render dynamic Mermaid diagrams into standalone SVG assets using mermaid-cli. Next, build_html_reader.py bundles the chapters into a self-contained, mobile-friendly HTML reader with offline math rendering and embedded CSS navigation.
tour.languageLesson: Pre-rendering Mermaid code blocks into static SVGs during build time eliminates client-side rendering latency and external CDN dependencies.

tour.title: Resilient PDF Compilation Engine
tour.description: Complementing the HTML reader, the build system provides a robust PDF compilation pipeline in build_pdf.py. Because headless browser printing frequently suffers from memory leaks and hung processes, the script implements bounded retries, detailed attempt logging, and POSIX process tree termination. Accompanying unit tests in test_build_pdf.py ensure that timeouts and process group kills behave reliably under simulated failures.
tour.languageLesson: In Python, terminating headless browser subtrees requires process group killing (os.killpg) to prevent orphaned renderer processes from consuming server memory.

tour.title: Typography and Rule Verification
tour.description: Publishing professional multilingual documentation requires strict formatting standards. The repository uses check_emphasis.py and check_project_rules.py to catch CommonMark syntax quirks around CJK punctuation, forbid volatile dates, and verify relative markdown links. The typography test suite in test_cjk_typography.py mechanically enforces character spacing boundaries and full-width punctuation across all chapters.

tour.title: Artifact Integrity and CI/CD Security
tour.description: The final stage links publication tooling, security auditing, and continuous deployment into an automated release pipeline. Before guides are published, verify_artifacts.py inspects document titles, PDF headers, and SHA-256 manifests, while ci.yaml runs automated tests and builds. Additionally, test_workflow_security.py audits GitHub Actions definitions to enforce immutable commit SHA pinning and minimal token permissions across all workflows.
tour.languageLesson: Securing CI/CD pipelines requires pinning GitHub Actions to immutable full-length commit SHAs and granting GITHUB_TOKEN minimal read-only permissions by default.
